newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot fuel oil prices lose more ground.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot fuel oil prices lose more ground.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices lost more ground Wednesday in lackluster activity, still pressured by crumbling crude, ample avails and sagging utility demand amid fairly competitive natgas prices, industry sources said.

"The market is down because everyone has barrels to sell, and with crude down this much, resid has to move lower," said one cash trader, adding bearish weather next week and sinking gas prices offered little hope for a resid rally near-term.
New York Harbor physical one percent skidded more than 50 cents to about the $16.50 a barrel area, with March paper down the same amount to $16.35-50 on softer crude, traders said.

Lower sulphurs remained pressured by competitive gas prices though New York city gates gained today on forecasts for one or two more days of cold. NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally tumbled another 75 cents or more to $18.25-50, with April HP paper reportedly done at $17.45.
High sulphurs in New York held relatively steady but underlying sentiment remained bearish. NYH March three percent paper sold at $13.60 versus prompt in the $15 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were about a quarter lower, with one percent now at $15.25-50 and three percent at $12.50.
Traders said expectations two USG coker units will be back later this week may limit further downside in HSFO prices.
New York city gate gas prices firmed 15 cents to about $3.05/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid fell to a $2.62/mmBtu equivalent.
